summary: Frederick A. Ober, a young American naturalist, spent 1876 to 1878 collecting birds in the Lesser Antilles for the Smithsonian Institution, and here tells of it island by island. Most of the book is about Dominica: camps in the forest with hunters and guides, the Boiling Lake, the Caribs of the windward coast and their language, and the hunt for the imperial parrot. He sails to St. Vincent in the hurricane season and camps in the crater of the Soufrière, stays on a sugar estate, goes on to Grenada and the Grenadines, hunts monkeys, and ends in Martinique, at the birthplace of the Empress Josephine, and on the Soufrière of Guadeloupe. An appendix by George N. Lawrence lists the birds of the islands and describes the new species Ober found.
